analysis_steps.goal: Prior-based CO(2-1) search at MUSE positions and redshifts

method.value: Gaussian line fits to single-pixel spectra from the 3'' tapered cube using a Bayesian MCMC

evidence.loc: 3.2 Additional sources with MUSE redshift priors at z < 2.9
evidence.quote: We then fit the lines with a Gaussian curve, using a custom-made Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo routine with the following priors:

key_parameters.value: Priors: velocity Gaussian sigma=100 km/s; width Maxwellian 100 km/s; flux Gaussian sigma=0.5 Jy km/s

evidence.loc: 3.2 Additional sources with MUSE redshift priors at z < 2.9
evidence.quote: *line flux*: a Gaussian distribution centered at zero, with $\sigma = 0.5$ Jy km s$^{-1}$, allowing both positive and negative line fluxes to be fitted.

key_parameters.value: Selection: S/N>3 in all three fits, |dv|<80 km/s, width>100 km/s

evidence.loc: 3.2 Additional sources with MUSE redshift priors at z < 2.9
evidence.quote: we select only the objects that have a velocity offset of $<80$ km s$^{-1}$ from the MUSE systemic redshift

fitting.value: Uncertainties from 16th and 84th percentiles of posteriors

evidence.loc: 3.2 Additional sources with MUSE redshift priors at z < 2.9
evidence.quote: The uncertainties are computed from the 16th and 84th percentiles of the posterior distributions of each parameter.

validation.value: Refit with broader width prior (200 km/s) and with uniform frequency prior over ±1 GHz

evidence.loc: 3.2 Additional sources with MUSE redshift priors at z < 2.9

analysis_steps.goal: Derive stellar mass, SFR, A_V from SED fitting

method.value: MAGPHYS high-z extension on UV-FIR photometry including ASPECS 1.2 and 3.0 mm

evidence.quote: we derive the SFR (and $M_{*}$ and $A_{V}$) from the UV-FIR data (including 24$\mu$m–160$\mu$m and ASPECS-LP 1.2 mm and 3.0 mm) using MAGPHYS

key_parameters.value: Zero-point errors added in quadrature, 5% error floor

evidence.quote: include a 5% error-floor to further account for systematic errors in the physical models (following (cite: Leja2018))
systematic uncertainties can be of order $\sim 0.3$ dex (cite: Conroy2013)
The code performs a Bayesian inference of the posterior likelihood distribution of the fitted parameter

analysis_steps.goal: Unobscured SFR and metallicity from MUSE lines

method.value: SFR([OII]) following Kewley2004 without dust correction; metallicity from [NeIII]/[OII] following Maiolino2008

evidence.quote: We derive SFRs from $\mathrm{[O\,\textsc{ii}]}\ \lambda 3726,3729$ following (cite: Kewley2004), adopting a (cite: Chabrier2003) IMF.
we instead adopt an average $\mathrm{[O\,\textsc{ii}]}\ \lambda 3726,3729$/$\mathrm{H}\alpha$ ratio of unity

validation.value: Compared with mass-metallicity relations of Maiolino2008 and Zahid2014

evidence.quote: They are all metal-rich and consistent with a solar or super-solar metallicity, in line with the expectations from the mass-metallicity relation.

analysis_steps.goal: Convert CO flux to molecular gas mass

evidence.quote: $\ensuremath{M_{\mathrm{mol}}}/\ensuremath{\mathrm{M}_{\odot}}= \left(\alpha_{\mathrm{CO}}/r_{J1}\right)

assumptions.value: alpha_CO = 3.6 Msun (K km/s pc^2)^-1; MS excitation ladder

evidence.quote: we use an $\ensuremath{\alpha_{\mathrm{CO}}}= 3.6$ $\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$)$^{-1}$, appropriate for star-forming galaxies
This choice of $\alpha_{\mathrm{CO}}$ is supported by our finding that the ASPECS-LP sources are mostly on the MS and have (near-)solar metallicity

assumptions.value: MS scatter 0.3 dex; MS reference from polynomial fit to rolling median at low z

evidence.quote: we show $\pm0.3$ dex scatter around a second order polynomial fit to the rolling median of the SFRs all the galaxies

validation.value: Compared with AGN fractions of Wang2017 and Haggard2010

evidence.quote: The AGN fractions found in ASPECS-LP are broadly consistent with these ranges given the limited numbers and considerable Poisson error.
